final_rationale: The verdict changes because the Actor narrowed the position to a caveated, disclosed, policy-bounded certification theory that better matches the admissible summary already in the record. No new admissible evidence was added. That distinction matters: the same evidence still does not support unqualified certification, does not show that no material weakness remains, and does not show an approved mitigation satisfying the policy elements. But on the current summary, a narrower conclusion is supportable: aggregate readiness is reported above threshold, no severity-one rehearsal incidents are reported, and the remaining weakness is described as identified and bounded. That is enough for compliant_with_caveats only if the action is explicitly conditioned on disclosure of the known limitation and not represented as limitation-free. The caveat is not merely rhetorical; it is the compliance predicate that keeps the position within policy bounds.
remaining_concerns: No genuinely new admissible evidence was provided; the accessible record remains summary-level only and key predicates cannot be independently verified from this role.
Compliance depends on the certification being explicitly caveated, with disclosure of the refund-workflow limitation; the actual certification language is still not in evidence.
There is still no admissible evidence of an approved mitigation package with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion.
The materiality of the remaining refund-policy summarization weakness is still asserted rather than independently demonstrated in the accessible record.
A draft runbook and future monitoring remain supportive only; they do not eliminate the current disclosure requirement absent approval.
